newsitem.title: CHINA: China activist warns Japan not to play with fire.
newsitem.headline: China activist warns Japan not to play with fire.

text.p: A leading Chinese anti-Japan activist on Wednesday warned Tokyo not to play with fire in a row over disputed islands in the East China Sea and said Japan owed a new blood debt for the death of a Hong Kong activist.

Vocal mainland campaigner Tong Zeng said in a letter to the Japanese embassy in Beijing that Japanese coast guard vessels had caused the death of Hong Kong protester David Chan, who drowned after leaping from a tanker into the sea to assert Chinese claims to the area.
A Japanese coast guard medical team was unable to revive Chan but saved the life of a co-protester who also jumped into the waters in defiance of a Japanese blockade of the islands.

"The Japanese government not only hasn't apologised or given compensation for its innumerable crimes during its (World War Two) invason of China, but today owes the Chinese people a new blood debt," Tong said in the letter, sent by fax to foreign news agencies.

Many Chinese have demanded that Japan pay compensation for its wartime atrocities but Beijing, which receives billions of dollars of soft loans a year from Tokyo, agreed officially in the 1970s not to seek such indemnities.
The islands, called the Diaoyus in Chinese and the Senkakus in Japanese, have been at the centre of a raging dispute between Beijing and Tokyo, both of which claim sovereignty.

Tong urged Tokyo to dismantle a lighthouse built by a right-wing Japanese group on one of the islands in July and warned against any attempt to stop a planned October 5 protest by Hong Kong and Taiwanese groups.
"We hope the Japanese government will take note of history and not play with fire (because) in the end it will only bring trouble on themselves," he wrote.
"If the Japanese government...brings about another death of a Hong Kong or Taiwanese compatriot, the whole of the Chinese people will never forgive you," he said.
